title: Why Polling on Gun Control Gets It Wrong

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责报道《纽约时报》每日时事通讯DealBook的商业与政策。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市DealBook峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以直接观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的真实对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得一个月的所有新闻内容访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家锁定收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔维内西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: Enough.
sentences.zh: 够了。

sentences.en: We should expand background checks to keep guns out of the hands of felons, fugitives, and those under restraining orders.
sentences.zh: 我们应该扩大背景调查，防止重罪犯、逃犯以及受限制令约束的人获得枪支。

sentences.en: In calling for Republicans to pass gun safety measures, like expanded background checks, Democrats point to polling that shows that most Americans support the idea.
sentences.zh: 在呼吁共和党人通过枪支安全法案（如扩大背景调查）时，民主党人指出民意调查显示大多数美国人支持这一想法。

sentences.en: Stronger background checks are something that the vast majority of Americans, including the majority of gun owners, agree on.
sentences.zh: 更严格的背景调查是绝大多数美国人（包括大多数枪支所有者）的共识。

sentences.en: But as my colleague Nate Cohn has found, the polling does not tell the whole story.
sentences.zh: 但正如我的同事内特·科恩所发现的那样，民意调查并没有说明全部情况。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月7日，星期二。

sentences.en: So, Nate, right now there's a bill in Congress that would expand background checks.
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，目前国会有一项旨在扩大背景调查的法案。

sentences.en: And Democrats are struggling to get the votes for it.
sentences.zh: 而民主党人正在为争取该法案的票数而苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And one of the things that they're saying is look at the polling.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在说的一点是，看看民调吧。

sentences.en: The vast majority of Americans are actually in favor of this.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数美国人实际上都是赞成这一点的。

sentences.en: It's popular.
sentences.zh: 这很受欢迎。

sentences.en: So why won't you vote for it?
sentences.zh: 那你们为什么不投赞成票呢？

sentences.en: So I guess my first question for you, Nate, is are the Democrats right?
sentences.zh: 所以我给你的第一个问题是，内特，民主党人说得对吗？

sentences.en: Do most Americans want background checks?
sentences.zh: 大多数美国人真的想要背景调查吗？

sentences.en: Maybe.
sentences.zh: 也许吧。

sentences.en: They are right about the polling.
sentences.zh: 他们在民调数据上是对的。

sentences.en: In the public polls, voters overwhelmingly say that they support expanded universal background checks.
sentences.zh: 在公开民调中，选民压倒性地表示他们支持扩大普遍背景调查。

sentences.en: Some polls show that over 90 percent of Americans support expanded background checks.
sentences.zh: 一些民调显示，超过90%的美国人支持扩大背景调查。

sentences.en: So they're not making it up.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不是在凭空捏造。

sentences.en: The polls do show a tremendous amount of public support for a lot of the measures that they're proposing.
sentences.zh: 民调确实显示公众对他们提出的许多措施有极高的支持度。

sentences.en: But it's a little more complicated than that because although it's true that voters overwhelmingly say they support background
sentences.zh: 但事情要复杂一些，因为尽管选民在民调中压倒性地表示支持背景

sentences.en: checks and polling, their votes are a little bit different.
sentences.zh: 调查，但他们的投票结果却有些不同。

sentences.en: When states have put gun control policies up to a vote in referendums and initiatives, the public has returned less than unanimous support.
sentences.zh: 当各州将控枪政策付诸全民公投和倡议表决时，公众并未给予一致的支持。

sentences.en: In fact, the support has been about as divided as a presidential election.
sentences.zh: 事实上，支持率的分化程度就像一场总统大选一样。

sentences.en: OK, so the polls are overwhelmingly in support.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以民调显示压倒性的支持。

sentences.en: But when it actually comes to voting on it, that's when a difference pops up.
sentences.zh: 但当真正进行投票表决时，分歧就出现了。

sentences.en: Is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是这个意思吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, the public support for background checks has been much more equivocal when voters have the opportunity to enact expanded background checks into law.
sentences.zh: 是的，当选民有机会将扩大的背景调查以法律形式颁布时，公众对背景调查的支持要含糊得多。

sentences.en: And I think the best examples come in
sentences.zh: 我认为最好的例子发生在

sentences.en: 2016 when there were three referendums put up to vote in California, Maine and Nevada, three states
sentences.zh: 2016年，当时加利福尼亚州、缅因州和内华达州这三个州进行了三项公投表决

sentences.en: that voted for Hillary Clinton in general election that proposed in different ways expanded background checks on guns or on ammunition purchases.
sentences.zh: 在总统大选中投票支持希拉里·克林顿的三个州，以不同方式提出了关于扩大枪支或弹药购买背景调查的提案。

sentences.en: And those initiatives, you would think, might have received overwhelming support based on national surveys.
sentences.zh: 根据全国性调查，你可能会认为这些提案会获得压倒性的支持。

sentences.en: But in the end, they basically fared about as well as Hillary Clinton did.
sentences.zh: 但最终，它们的基本表现和希拉里·克林顿差不多。

sentences.en: And overall, the initiatives fared a little worse than she did.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，这些提案的表现甚至比她还要稍差一些。

sentences.en: So there wasn't unanimous support at all.
sentences.zh: 因此，根本没有出现全票支持的情况。

sentences.en: It was a deeply divided election that closely resembled the typical issue in national politics, not a matter of broad national consensus.
sentences.zh: 这是一场分歧严重的选举，非常类似于全国政治中的典型议题，而不是一个达成广泛全国共识的问题。

sentences.en: OK, so the expectation was that these background check bills would do really well, but actually they didn't.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以大家的预期是这些背景调查法案会表现得非常好，但实际上并没有。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In Maine, the background check bill actually loSt. It was defeated at the polls, even in the state where Hillary Clinton won narrowly.
sentences.zh: 在缅因州，背景调查法案实际上失败了。它在投票中被否决了，甚至在一个希拉里·克林顿险胜的州也是如此。

sentences.en: Well, in Nevada, it barely squeaked by.
sentences.zh: 而在内华达州，它只是勉强过关。

sentences.en: It was like a one point race.
sentences.zh: 就像是一场一个百分点的竞选。

sentences.en: That's also a battleground state.
sentences.zh: 那也是一个摇摆州。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton won it by a couple of points.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿以几个百分点的优势赢了那里。

sentences.en: In California, it won by a more comfortable margin.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州，它的获胜优势更舒适一些。

sentences.en: But, you know, we got more than 60 percent of the vote.
sentences.zh: 但你知道的，我们获得了超过60%的选票。

sentences.en: But, you know, so did Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 不过，你知道的，希拉里·克林顿也是。

sentences.en: So it's not it's it did about as well as you would expect for a partisan political issue.
sentences.zh: 所以它表现得就像你对一个党派政治议题的预期一样。

sentences.en: If nationwide background checks really have 80 or 90 percent support, then California, you might think, could be like 95 percent support or something.
sentences.zh: 如果全国范围内的背景调查真的有80%或90%的支持率，那么你可能会认为加利福尼亚州的支持率会达到95%左右。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there it is polling again, like a typical Democrat Republican issue.
sentences.zh: 而在这里，民调结果再次表现得像一个典型的民主党对共和党议题。

sentences.en: So, Nate, I guess on background check referendums, then far fewer voters say they wanted these rules than actually told pollsters.
sentences.zh: 所以，内特，我想在背景调查公投中，说自己想要这些规则的选民人数，要远少于实际告诉民调人员的人数。

sentences.en: So there's a huge difference between the share of people voting for the thing and the share of people saying they liked it in the poll.
sentences.zh: 因此，投票支持该法案的人数比例与在民调中表示喜欢它的人数比例之间存在巨大差异。

sentences.en: So I guess then that says to me that it's really just not as simple as the Democrats are making it seem.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这对我来说说明了，事情绝对不像民主党人表现得那么简单。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's certainly more complicated and it complicates a lot of the Democratic argument about how our government responds to gun violence.
sentences.zh: 是的，这肯定更复杂，并且使民主党人关于我们政府如何应对枪支暴力的许多论点变得复杂。

sentences.en: The Democratic contention is that, well, if the public overwhelmingly supports background
sentences.zh: 民主党人的论点是，如果公众压倒性地支持背景

sentences.en: checks and increased gun control measures, then there must be a host of other explanations that
sentences.zh: 调查和加强控枪措施，那么一定有一系列其他解释

sentences.en: help make sense of why legislation is consistently blocked in Washington and why Republicans choose to oppose these background checks anyway.
sentences.zh: 来帮助理解为什么立法在华盛顿屡屡受阻，以及为什么共和党人无论如何都要选择反对这些背景调查。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's the idea that the NRA and the gun lobby play a huge role in influencing senators in the back room or that's the composition of the
sentences.zh: 你知道，有一种观点认为美国步枪协会和枪支游说集团在幕后对参议员施加了巨大影响，或者是

sentences.en: Senate, which is tilted overwhelmingly toward more rural states or that there are single issue voters
sentences.zh: 参议院的构成严重倾向于更多乡村州，或者是有单一议题选民

sentences.en: that are getting in the way of the broader electorate support for background checks.
sentences.zh: 阻碍了广大选民对背景调查的支持。

sentences.en: I mean, all those theories may have some degree of merit or another, but, you know, if the electorate in
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，所有这些理论可能都有一定程度的道理，但是，如果在

sentences.en: several blue states basically returns a result that looks like a typical Democrat versus Republican
sentences.zh: 几个蓝州最终得出的结果看起来像是一场典型的民主党对阵共和党

sentences.en: election, it raises the possibility that the public is just simply more divided on this issue than the polls have made it seem.
sentences.zh: 选举，这就引发了一种可能性，即公众在这个问题上的分歧实际上比民调表现出来的要大得多。

sentences.en: Okay, so Nate, explain why it would be that the polls differ so much from the referenduMs. What's going on there?
sentences.zh: 好的，内特，请解释一下为什么民调结果会与公投结果相差这么大？这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Well, there are a lot of reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，原因有很多。

sentences.en: I mean, there sort of has to be to cover such a huge gap between these results in the national polls, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为了涵盖全国民调中如此巨大的差距，必须得有这些原因，对吧？

sentences.en: The first one is just that the polls could overstate the support for background checks.
sentences.zh: 第一个原因就是民调可能夸大了对背景调查的支持。

sentences.en: One of the most likely reasons is a phenomenon called acquiescence bias.
sentences.zh: 最可能的原因之一是一种被称为顺从偏差的现象。

sentences.en: Oh, what's that?
sentences.zh: 哦，那是什么？

sentences.en: I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: But it's just the tendency for people to sort of say yes to things.
sentences.zh: 但这只是一种人们倾向于对事物说“好”的倾向。

sentences.en: I mean, if you've ever nodded along with someone like I'm doing right now, like you're doing right now just to go
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你曾经点头附和过某人，就像我现在正在做的那样，就像你现在正在做的那样，只是为了顺着

sentences.en: along with it, or you've gone along with someone's idea for dinner and you were sort of agnostic about the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 别人的意思，或者你顺从了某人关于晚餐的想法，而你对那家餐厅其实无所谓。

sentences.en: I mean, those are all just real world examples of acquiescence bias.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是顺从偏差的现实生活中的例子。

sentences.en: And it plays out in polling too.
sentences.zh: 它在民调中也会起作用。

sentences.en: If there's an idea that just sort of sounds good, that's easy to go along with, something as reasonable sounding as a background check, I don't think it should be too surprising
sentences.zh: 如果有一个听起来很不错、很容易顺从的想法，比如像背景调查这样听起来很合理的金点子，我认为有一群人在

sentences.en: that there are a bunch of people who maybe if they thought about it a little harder could come down against it, who start out saying in a survey that they're for it.
sentences.zh: 仔细思考后可能会反对，但一开始却在调查中表示支持，这其实不应该太令人惊讶。

sentences.en: And another reason is that people sometimes just don't entirely understand the question.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是人们有时并不能完全理解问题。

sentences.en: I mean, imagine that you're taking a political poll on your phone and you're walking around the room and you're distracted a little bit, you're paying half attention.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想象一下你在手机上参与一项政治民调，你一边在房间里走来走去，一边有点分心，只有一半的注意力。

sentences.en: And the pollster asks you whether you support an expanded universal background check program.
sentences.zh: 而民调人员问你是否支持扩大的普遍背景调查计划。

sentences.en: And you heard background checks and you know you like the idea of background checks, but have you really determined that what we're really asking about here is a brand new
sentences.zh: 你听到了背景调查，你知道你喜欢背景调查的想法，但是你真的确定我们在这里真正询问的是一个全新的、

sentences.en: expanded federal background check program that's distinct from the one that already exists?
sentences.zh: 与现有计划不同的扩大联邦背景调查计划吗？

sentences.en: Maybe not.
sentences.zh: 也许并没有。

sentences.en: There could be people that, you know, want to indicate their general support for a background check program, but don't necessarily support some new initiative
sentences.zh: 有些人可能只是想表达他们对背景调查计划的总体支持，但不一定支持超越现行法律的任何新倡议

sentences.en: beyond what's already been enacted into law.
sentences.zh: 超越已经立法的内容。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: You know, a third thing is that the polls could miss an important dimension of public opinion,
sentences.zh: 你知道，第三点是民调可能忽略了公众舆论的一个重要维度，

sentences.en: and that's a status quo bias, a lowercase c conservative tendency to defer to the status quo and keep things the way they are when the stakes are high.
sentences.zh: 那就是现状偏差，一种小写的c保守倾向，即在利害攸关时倾向于顺从现状并保持原状。

sentences.en: A poll is really carefree.
sentences.zh: 民调确实是无忧无虑的。

sentences.en: It is easy to say you support Medicare for all.
sentences.zh: 说你支持全民医疗保险很容易。

sentences.en: It's easy to say that you support, you know, a $5 trillion
sentences.zh: 说你支持，你知道的，一个5万亿美元的

sentences.en: Green New Deal.
sentences.zh: 绿色新政也很容易。

sentences.en: But when that is actually about to become a reality and all of the real world consequences and responsibility come with it, voters could choose to be a lot more cautious about
sentences.zh: 但当这真正即将成为现实，并且伴随着所有现实世界的后果和责任时，选民可能会选择对

sentences.en: enacting those same policies into law or supporting candidates who would really do those things than
sentences.zh: 将这些相同的政策立法，或者支持真正会做这些事情的候选人保持谨慎得多，

sentences.en: they would be about just simply indicating a general support for the idea in a poll when there are no stakes.
sentences.zh: 而这与他们在没有利害关系时，在民调中仅仅表示对该想法的普遍支持相比，态度会完全不同。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But this seems to be discrepancies and problems with polling that apply to everything, right?
sentences.zh: 但这似乎是适用于所有事情的民调差异和问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Where do guns specifically fit into this?
sentences.zh: 枪支具体是怎么契合这一点的呢？

sentences.en: So I think you're right that everything I've said so far could be said to apply for almost every issue.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为你是对的，我到目前为止所说的一切都可以说适用于几乎所有议题。

sentences.en: And clearly what we see on these gun control referendums is an order of magnitude bigger than the typical issue, right?
sentences.zh: 显然，我们在这些控枪公投上看到的差距比典型议题要大一个数量级，对吧？

sentences.en: 90% support just almost entirely evaporating in Republican areas.
sentences.zh: 90%的支持率在共和党地区几乎完全蒸发。

sentences.en: That says that there's something more going on here.
sentences.zh: 这说明这里面还有更多深层次的原因。

sentences.en: And I think that the more that's going on is that about half the public has this deep connection to gun rights and supports gun rights and that a political campaign can activate
sentences.zh: 我认为更多深层次的原因是，大约有一半公众对枪支权利有着深厚的联系并支持枪支权利，而政治竞选可以激活

sentences.en: that support and quickly flip voters who initially say they support background checks to oppose background checks by drawing on their deeper sympathy for gun rights.
sentences.zh: 这种支持，并通过唤起他们对枪支权利更深层的同情，迅速将最初表示支持背景调查的选民变成反对背景调查。

sentences.en: And so I think that that can play out in several different ways.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这可以通过几种不同的方式体现出来。

sentences.en: One is that there can just be a broad campaign.
sentences.zh: 一种是可能存在一场广泛的竞选活动。

sentences.en: You can imagine there's political advertisement ahead of the election where the NRA says that this background check initiative
sentences.zh: 你可以想象在选举前会有政治广告，美国步枪协会在广告中称这项背景调查提案

sentences.en: is going to take away your guns and part of taking away your gun rights and it's a threat to the Second
sentences.zh: 将会剥夺你的枪支，这是剥夺你枪支权利的一部分，是对第二修正案的威胁。

sentences.en: Amendment.
sentences.zh: 修正案。

sentences.en: And then suddenly all of these Republicans who were initially fine with the idea may see it as part of some larger threat and then come to oppose the initiative.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，所有这些最初对这个想法持无所谓态度的共和党人可能会将其视为某种更大威胁的一部分，进而开始反对这项提案。

sentences.en: And that wouldn't prove the polls were wrong, strictly speaking.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，这并不证明民调是错的。

sentences.en: You know, people change their mind.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们会改变主意。

sentences.en: Their view might have been genuine in the first place, but the voters came to see what seemed at first to be a narrow background check initiative as
sentences.zh: 他们的观点最初可能是真诚的，但选民后来开始将起初看起来微不足道的背景调查提案视为

sentences.en: part of a broader campaign to restrict gun rights, which they care more about.
sentences.zh: 限制枪支权利更广泛运动的一部分，而他们更在乎枪支权利。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And we know from other polls that nearly half of Americans are strong supporters of gun rights and don't really support increased gun restrictions and so on.
sentences.zh: 我们从其他民调中得知，近一半的美国人是枪支权利的坚定支持者，并不真正支持增加枪支限制等等。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that if a campaign can tap into those feelings, that they could very quickly polarize a political debate on this issue.
sentences.zh: 所以这就说得通了，如果一场竞选活动能够利用这些情绪，他们就能非常迅速地将这个议题上的政治辩论两极化。

sentences.en: Another way it can play out is, you know, that there could be voters who support initiatives in the abstract, but don't necessarily support a specific proposal.
sentences.zh: 另一种表现形式是，你知道，可能会有一些选民在抽象意义上支持提案，但不一定支持具体的提案。

sentences.en: They might find, you know, the expression that the devils are in the details.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会发现，俗话说得好，魔鬼藏在细节里。

sentences.en: They might find that the specifics of the initiative are not exactly to their liking.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会发现提案的具体细节并不完全合他们的心意。

sentences.en: Transferring guns between friends is an example of something that came up in Maine.
sentences.zh: 在朋友之间转让枪支就是缅因州出现过的一个例子。

sentences.en: You might say you support universal background checks in a poll, but maybe you reconsider when you find out that means
sentences.zh: 你可能会在民调中说你支持普遍背景调查，但也许当你发现这意味着

sentences.en: you can't give a gun to your friend before a hunting trip without having to take it to a third party for a background check.
sentences.zh: 在打猎前你不能把枪借给朋友，除非把它送到第三方那里进行背景调查时，你就会重新考虑。

sentences.en: That suddenly seems like an inconvenience that you wouldn't be willing to go along with.
sentences.zh: 这突然看起来成了一种你不愿意接受的麻烦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And it's worth stepping back to consider how all of these different factors,
sentences.zh: 退一步考虑所有这些不同的因素是如何相互作用的，是非常值得的，

sentences.en: deference to the status quo, you know, a campaign about gun rights, and then a focus on the details of the initiative all really work together.
sentences.zh: 顺从现状，你知道的，关于枪支权利的竞选，然后是对提案细节的关注，所有这些确实都在共同起作用。

sentences.en: You have this big group of voters who told a pollster that they support expanded background checks, even though they support gun rights.
sentences.zh: 你有这样一大群选民，他们告诉民调人员他们支持扩大背景调查，尽管他们也支持枪支权利。

sentences.en: And given that underlying support for gun rights, all of these little issues, the details that might, you know,
sentences.zh: 鉴于对枪支权利的这种潜在支持，所有这些小问题，这些细节可能会

sentences.en: lead them to believe there's a bigger threat to gun rights than they thought when they heard about this idea
sentences.zh: 导致他们相信枪支权利面临的威胁比他们在抽象层面上听到这个想法时想象的要大，

sentences.en: in the abstract, and then a campaign that's reinforcing it that all, I think, naturally coalesces
sentences.zh: 再加上一场强化这种看法的竞选活动，我认为所有这些自然地凝聚在一起，

sentences.en: into a very easy choice for them to say no and defer cautiously to keeping the status quo as it is.
sentences.zh: 让他们非常容易做出选择：说不，并谨慎地顺从于保持现状不变。

sentences.en: So despite the fact that voters might be inclined to support some form of gun control, they can also be open to campaigns that appeal to gun rights, right?
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管选民可能倾向于支持某种形式的控枪，但他们也可能容易受到呼吁枪支权利的竞选活动的影响，对吧？

sentences.en: Because a number of those voters support gun rights, I mean, a lot of them are gun owners.
sentences.zh: 因为其中相当一部分选民支持枪支权利，我的意思是，他们当中很多人都是枪支持有者。

sentences.en: So when someone like the NRA says background checks are a slippery slope and a fundamental challenge to gun rights, those same people will vote no on the referendum.
sentences.zh: 所以当像美国步枪协会这样的人说背景调查是滑向深渊的开始，是对枪支权利的根本挑战时，同样这批人就会在公投中投反对票。

sentences.en: That's certainly how it's played out to this point.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，情况确实一直是这样的。

sentences.en: Okay, so Nate, that sounds like that's the answer, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，内特，听上去这就是答案对吧？

sentences.en: That there's a really good reason why Republicans aren't voting for this background check bill.
sentences.zh: 也就是为什么共和党人没有投票支持这项背景调查法案，其实是有个非常好的原因的。

sentences.en: The data shows they shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 数据表明他们不应该投。

sentences.en: People don't actually want it in those huge numbers that the polls suggeSt.
sentences.zh: 人们其实并没有像民调显示的那么多的人数真正想要它。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that members of Congress would be afraid that if they did vote for the background check bill, they'd be voted out of office.
sentences.zh: 所以国会议员们会担心，如果他们真的投票支持背景调查法案，就会在选举中被投票赶下台，这也就说得通了。

sentences.en: Well, not exactly.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不完全是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, they may be right to think that their districts oppose new background check or gun control legislation, but they may not be right that they would suffer
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们认为自己的选区反对新的背景调查或枪支管控立法可能是对的，但他们不一定会遭受

sentences.en: a severe political cost if they did support background checks themselves.
sentences.zh: 如果他们自己真的支持背景调查，就会付出沉重的政治代价。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用，即可获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Nate, we established that polling really overestimates how supportive the public is on an issue like background checks.
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，我们确定了民调确实大大高估了公众对背景调查这类议题的支持程度。

sentences.en: But you also just said that that doesn't necessarily mean that Republicans should be afraid of losing their seat if they try to support it.
sentences.zh: 但你刚才也说过，这并不一定意味着如果共和党人试图支持它，就应该害怕失去席位。

sentences.en: So explain that.
sentences.zh: 所以请解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: Well, there's a difference between whether someone has a view about an issue, like say they oppose background checks,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里有一个区别：一个人是对某个议题有某种看法，比如比方说他们反对背景调查，

sentences.en: and whether they feel so strongly about an issue that they are likelier to vote against a candidate because that candidate disagrees with them on that issue.
sentences.zh: 与他们对某个议题的感受是否强烈到更倾向于投票反对某个候选人，因为该候选人在那个议题上与他们意见不一致。

sentences.en: We sometimes refer to a group of people called single-issue voters to describe a group of voters who feel so strongly about something like guns or abortion
sentences.zh: 我们有时会用“单一议题选民”这个词来形容这样一群选民：他们对诸如枪支或堕胎之类的事情感觉非常强烈，

sentences.en: that it's essentially the only issue in the campaign for them once it becomes live in the race.
sentences.zh: 以至于一旦这个议题在竞选中变得活跃，对他们来说它基本上就是竞选中的唯一议题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in this case, a single-issue voter might be someone who supports gun rights and maybe is open to voting for Democrats or Republicans,
sentences.zh: 所以在这种情况下，“单一议题选民”可能是指那些支持枪支权利、也许对投票给民主党或共和党持开放态度的人，

sentences.en: but there's no chance that they would vote for a candidate who supported background checks.
sentences.zh: 但他们绝对不可能投票给支持背景调查的候选人。

sentences.en: And the truth is that it is not easy to measure the share of the electorate that might count as a single-issue voter on guns.
sentences.zh: 而事实是，要衡量在枪支问题上可能算作单一议题选民的选民比例并不容易。

sentences.en: It's a difficult question to study, and it would be even harder to arrive at those sort of figures for every congressional district in the country.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很难研究的问题，要为全国每一个国会选区得出这种类型的数据就更难了。

sentences.en: And why is it so difficult to measure?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么难衡量？

sentences.en: Well, for one thing, it suffers from some of the same problems that we described at the beginning for issue polling.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一方面，它受到我们在开头为议题民调所描述的某些相同问题的影响。

sentences.en: Like, acquiescence bias.
sentences.zh: 比如，顺从偏差。

sentences.en: It's very easy to tell a pollster, oh, there's no way I'm ever going to support someone who disagrees with me on X, Y, and Z issues.
sentences.zh: 告诉民调人员“哦，我绝对不可能支持在X、Y、Z议题上与我意见不合的人”，这非常容易。

sentences.en: But it's harder to know whether that's actually true in practice.
sentences.zh: 但很难知道这在实践中是否真的是这样。

sentences.en: And there's a long history of voters telling pollsters, say, that they could never vote for someone who disagrees with them on abortion.
sentences.zh: 而且有很长一段时间的历史表明，选民会告诉民调人员，比方说他们绝不会投票给在堕胎问题上与自己意见不合的人。

sentences.en: But then they come around and they support, say, a candidate from their own party who has the opposite view of them on abortion.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们回心转意，去支持了比方说他们自己党内的一位候选人，而该候选人在堕胎问题上的观点与他们相反。

sentences.en: Now, that may be because those voters don't know that that candidate has a different view on them on abortion.
sentences.zh: 现在，这可能是因为这些选民不知道该候选人在堕胎问题上与他们的看法不同。

sentences.en: It may be because both candidates in the race in that instance may oppose the voters' view on abortion.
sentences.zh: 这可能是因为那种情况下竞选中的两位候选人可能都反对选民对堕胎的看法。

sentences.en: Or it may be that they are just overstating it because it's much easier to tell a pollster that you're going to do something than to actually do it.
sentences.zh: 或者也可能是因为他们只是在夸大其词，因为告诉民调人员你要去做某事，比实际去做要容易得多。

sentences.en: Okay, so because this is such a hard thing to measure, if you're a Republican senator right now and you're looking at the data, you're looking at the polling,
sentences.zh: 好吧，既然这是一个如此难以衡量的问题，如果你现在是一名共和党参议员，并且你在查看数据、查看民调，

sentences.en: plus all the real votes on this issue, you don't actually know whether people would vote you out of office if you supported the background check bill in Congress right now.
sentences.zh: 再加上关于这个议题的所有真实投票，你其实并不知道如果现在你在国会支持背景调查法案，人们是否会把你投票赶下台。

sentences.en: So then why does it feel like politicians are still making the calculation not to stick their necks out of this issue, like not to support the bill?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么感觉政治家们仍在做着这样的算计：不在这个议题上冒险出头，比如不支持这项法案？

sentences.en: Well, some might be generally opposed to gun control initiatives,
sentences.zh: 嗯，有些人可能普遍反对枪支管控倡议，

sentences.en: but even stipulating that they are open to background checks or other gun control laws except for their concerns about the political fallout.
sentences.zh: 但即使假设他们对背景调查或其他枪支管控法律持开放态度，只是担心政治后果。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it's fair to say that they're not wrong to be worried about a backlash if they cross their party's base on this issue.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为可以公平地说，如果他们在这个问题上违背了党内基础选民，担心会遭到强烈反弹，这并不是错误的。

sentences.en: It may not be very clear in the data, but I mean, we can use our common sense here.
sentences.zh: 数据可能不是很明显，但我的意思是，我们在这里可以运用常识。

sentences.en: You know, in today's polarized partisan environment, going against your party's base is all but certain to provoke a major political backlash.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在当今两极分化的党派环境中，违背你所在党派的基础选民几乎铁定会引发重大的政治反弹。

sentences.en: I don't know whether it's enough for them to lose a primary election, but it could be enough to court a primary challenge.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是否足以让他们在初选中落败，但它可能足以招致一次初选挑战。

sentences.en: And even if not that, it's enough to make many of your usual allies upset and angry with you.
sentences.zh: 即便不是那样，这也足以让许多你平日里的盟友对你感到不安和愤怒。

sentences.en: Republicans don't run for office because they want to fight with conservatives.
sentences.zh: 共和党人竞选公职不是因为他们想和保守派斗争。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you were to reverse it and you imagine what a moderate Democrat might feel if they were to come out on the pro-life side or, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你反过来想象一下，一个温和派民主党人如果现在表态支持反堕胎一方，或者你知道的，

sentences.en: anti-Roe versus Wade side of things right now,
sentences.zh: 也就是反对罗伊诉韦德案的一方，他们会有什么感受，

sentences.en: just imagine what their lives would be like in terms of all of the people who they usually count as their allies being really upset at them.
sentences.zh: 只要想象一下他们的生活会是什么样，身边所有平时被他们视为盟友的人都对他们非常生气。

sentences.en: And, you know, so it doesn't surprise me.
sentences.zh: 所以呢，这并不让我感到意外。

sentences.en: You're going against your team, right?
sentences.zh: 你在违背你的团队，对吧？

sentences.en: Your friends are going to stop talking to you.
sentences.zh: 你的朋友们会不再跟你说话。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And even if it's not as bad as I just described, I mean, for most of these members of Congress, their jobs are easy.
sentences.zh: 而且即使情况不像我刚才描述的那样糟糕，我的意思是，对大多数这些国会议员来说，他们的工作是很轻松的。

sentences.en: They don't have serious general election campaigns oftentimes.
sentences.zh: 他们通常没有激烈的全国大选竞选。

sentences.en: They don't usually have strong primary challenges, at least if they go along with their party's base on, you know, hot-button issues like this one.
sentences.zh: 他们通常没有强有力的初选挑战，至少如果他们在诸如此类的高度敏感议题上顺从党内基础选民的话。

sentences.en: And so you're talking about the difference between them having a nice,
sentences.zh: 所以你谈论的是两种情况之间的区别：一种是在华盛顿拥有美好、

sentences.en: comfortable time in Washington and having a lot of deeply unpleasant interactions with people who you usually count as your friends and allies.
sentences.zh: 舒适的时光，另一种则是与那些你通常视为朋友和盟友的人发生大量极其不愉快的互动。

sentences.en: I think we have a really telling recent example in the case of Chris Jacobs, a congressman from upstate New York near Buffalo, who, after the mass shooting there,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在克里斯·雅各布斯的案例中有一个非常能说明问题的近期例子，他是纽约州北部靠近布法罗的一名国会议员，在那里的惨剧发生后，

sentences.en: came out in support of a federal assault weapons ban.
sentences.zh: 他公开表示支持联邦攻击性武器禁令。

sentences.en: And there was an intense backlash against him from, you know, local Republican Party leaders and activists.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是来自当地共和党领导层和积极分子的强烈反对。

sentences.en: And he decided in just one week that he wasn't even going to run for re-election.
sentences.zh: 仅仅在一周之内，他就决定甚至不参加连任竞选了。

sentences.en: His polling said that he could have run for re-election, but it just wasn't worth it.
sentences.zh: 他的民调显示他本可以竞选连任，但根本不值得这样做。

sentences.en: This isn't what he signed up for.
sentences.zh: 这不是他所期望的。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to have some big fight with, you know, his allies and fellow conservatives over this issue.
sentences.zh: 他不想为了这个议题与他的盟友和同为保守派的人产生什么大冲突。

sentences.en: And it was easier for him to step out of the ring.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，退出角逐要容易得多。

sentences.en: That's a pretty dramatic conclusion, that there was just no hope at all, so he just quit.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当戏剧性的结论，即完全没有希望了，所以他就直接放弃了。

sentences.en: Yeah, one thing I'll say is, you know, we, as, you know, non-politicians, we often from the outside, you know, want them to fight.
sentences.zh: 对，我要说的一点是，你知道，我们作为非政治人物，往往从局外人的角度，希望他们去战斗。

sentences.en: And there are all sorts of issues where politicians are very happy to fight.
sentences.zh: 而且在各种各样的议题上，政治家们非常乐意去战斗。

sentences.en: You know, they want to fight for things that they care really deeply about, that align with their party's base,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们想要为那些他们极为关心的、符合党内基础选民的事情而战，

sentences.en: where they fight against their normal adversaries and the people that they dislike.
sentences.zh: 在这些事情上，他们与平时的对手以及他们不喜欢的人进行战斗。

sentences.en: But in this case, you're asking a Republican not to fight against the people that they don't like with their usual allies,
sentences.zh: 但在这种情况下，你要求一个共和党人不要和他们不喜欢的人战斗、而是与他们平时的盟友战斗，

sentences.en: but to fight against the people who usually count as their friends.
sentences.zh: 而是去和那些通常被视为朋友的人战斗。

sentences.en: And I think that when you see just how quickly that they decide to peel away in that sort of setting, it gives you, you know, some sense of how unpleasant that is for them,
sentences.zh: 我认为，当你看到他们在那种环境下决定抽身离开的速度有多快时，你就会对这对他有多么不愉快有一些体会，

sentences.en: even if they could win in the end.
sentences.zh: 即使他们最终可能会赢。

sentences.en: So that's an example of a politician reading the tea leaves, anticipating probably that he might be voted out because he bucked the party line, and dropping out.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一个政治家看风使舵的例子，他预料到自己可能会因为违背党派路线而被投票赶下台，于是便退出了。

sentences.en: But are there examples of Republicans supporting gun control measures and not getting voted out?
sentences.zh: 但是，有没有共和党人支持枪支管控措施而没有被投票赶下台的例子呢？

sentences.en: I mean, are there counterexamples?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有没有反例？

sentences.en: I mean, I think the easiest counterexample is to look at Pat Toomey.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为最简单的反例就是看看帕特·图米。

sentences.en: You may recall that after the mass shooting at Sandy Hook Elementary School in late 2012, there was this bipartisan bill to create background checks.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，在2012年底桑迪胡克小学枪击案发生后，曾有过一项旨在建立背景调查的两党法案。

sentences.en: And it was sponsored most notably by Joe Manchin, but also by Senate Republican Pat Toomey.
sentences.zh: 该法案最引人注目的是由乔·曼钦发起的，但也得到了参议院共和党人帕特·图米的支持。

sentences.en: It was the Manchin-Toomey bill, and that bill did not overcome a Senate filibuster, but it did earn the support of several Senate Republicans.
sentences.zh: 这就是曼钦-图米法案，该法案没有通过参议院的冗长辩论阻挠，但它确实赢得了几位参议院共和党人的支持。

sentences.en: And none of those Senate Republicans appeared to face a serious primary challenge because of their support for that bill.
sentences.zh: 而且这些参议院共和党人似乎并没有因为支持该法案而面临严峻的初选挑战。

sentences.en: Pat Toomey, in fact, didn't even face a primary challenge at all in 2016.
sentences.zh: 事实上，帕特·图米在2016年甚至根本没有面临初选挑战。

sentences.en: His Republican primary was uncontested.
sentences.zh: 他的共和党初选是无竞争的。

sentences.en: So clearly, it's at least possible to support this kind of law and avoid any serious political costs for it.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，支持这种法律并避免任何重大的政治代价至少是可能的。

sentences.en: Now, I can think of some arguments for why Pat Toomey, being from Pennsylvania, meant he was a little less likely to face a backlash than maybe if he was, you know,
sentences.zh: 现在，我可以想到一些理由来解释为什么帕特·图米来自宾夕法尼亚州，这意味着他面临反弹的可能性比他如果是个

sentences.en: the senator from Wyoming or something.
sentences.zh: 怀俄明州或其他地方的参议员要小一些。

sentences.en: But nonetheless,
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，

sentences.en: the absence of any obvious primary challenge there suggests that it's by no means inevitable that backing these laws will result in a political disaster for a Republican.
sentences.zh: 那里没有任何明显的初选挑战表明，支持这些法律绝不意味着会给共和党人带来政治灾难。

sentences.en: So, Nate, what does that tell you?
sentences.zh: 那么，内特，这说明了什么？

sentences.en: And what should Republican senators take away from that?
sentences.zh: 共和党参议员应该从中吸取什么教训？

sentences.en: I think that my simple answer is that this is really hard to predict.
sentences.zh: 我认为我简单的回答是，这真的很难预测。

sentences.en: You look at what happened to Chris Jacobs, and he obviously faced an immediate and widespread backlash for coming out in support of federal assault weapons ban.
sentences.zh: 看看克里斯·雅各布斯遭遇了什么，他显然因为公开支持联邦攻击性武器禁令而面临了即时且广泛的反弹。

sentences.en: Pat Toomey, on the other hand, did not face that kind of a backlash.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，帕特·图米并没有面临那种反弹。

sentences.en: Clearly, there's some risk there, but it's not inevitable either.
sentences.zh: 很显然，这里存在一定的风险，但这也不是必然发生的。

sentences.en: I do think that coming out in support of background checks is a lot less risky for Republicans than coming out in favor of an assault gun ban.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为，对于共和党人来说，公开支持背景调查比公开支持攻击性武器禁令要风险小得多。

sentences.en: After all, those polls do show 90% support for background checks where we began this episode.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我们本集节目开头的那些民调确实显示有90%的人支持背景调查。

sentences.en: And while many of those people may not support it terribly strongly, like the fact that they're willing to say that they support it when they first hear about it,
sentences.zh: 虽然其中许多人可能支持得并不是非常强烈，比如他们一听到这个消息就愿意表示支持这一事实，

sentences.en: to me that betrays that maybe the political costs of coming out in support of that are probably not that grave for a Republican like Pat Toomey.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这暴露了对于像帕特·图米这样的共和党人来说，站出来支持这一立场的政治代价可能并不是那么严重。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, even if they wouldn't vote for it on a referendum.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使他们在全民公投中不会投票支持它。

sentences.en: Yeah, even if it's not something they like enough to support, it can't be that poisonous and toxic to support if most Republicans, when they first hear the idea,
sentences.zh: 对，即使这不是他们喜欢到愿意支持的程度，但如果大多数共和党人在第一次听到这个想法时，

sentences.en: say they'll support it.
sentences.zh: 都说他们会支持，那么支持它就不可能是那么有毒和具有毁灭性的。

sentences.en: Now, that might be a little bit different in this context with Democrats pushing the bill,
sentences.zh: 现在，在民主党人推动该法案的背景下，情况可能会略有不同，

sentences.en: which I think will automatically polarize it to some extent compared to in a poll question where it's just sort of presented as this abstract idea from nowhere.
sentences.zh: 我认为，与那种只被作为凭空出现的抽象概念提出的民调问题相比，这在某种程度上会自动使其两极分化。

sentences.en: I would guess that if we had a poll about do you support the bill backed by House Democrats and Joe Biden to enact new restrictions on guns,
sentences.zh: 我猜，如果我们做一个关于“你是否支持由众议院民主党人和乔·拜登支持的旨在对枪支实施新限制的法案”的民调，

sentences.en: that that would fare pretty poorly among Republicans or at least quite a bit worse.
sentences.zh: 那它在共和党人中的反响会相当糟糕，或者至少会糟糕得多。

sentences.en: Because it's associated with the other team.
sentences.zh: 因为这与对方阵营联系在一起。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But I think that in the scheme of issues that those initial numbers on the strong public support for background checks suggest to me that there are a huge number of Republican-leaning voters who will not automatically dismiss them because they heard that they supported a background check law.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在各种议题的计划中，公众对背景调查强力支持的初始数据向我表明，有大量倾向于共和党选民不会仅仅因为听说他们支持背景调查法案就自动予以驳回。

sentences.en: So it sounds like what you're saying is there are voters who would vote against this on a referendum, but who would not necessarily punish their member of Congress,
sentences.zh: 听起来你的意思是，有些选民会在全民公投中对此投反对票，但他们不一定会惩罚自己的国会议员，

sentences.en: with whom they agree on most other things, right, for supporting background checks.
sentences.zh: 即那些他们在几乎所有其他事情上都意见一致的议员，对吧，不会因为他们支持背景调查而惩罚他们。

sentences.en: So I guess the question is, are there enough Republicans in Congress who are willing to take that risk and count on those voters not to punish them?
sentences.zh: 所以我想问题在于，国会中是否有足够多的共和党人愿意承担这种风险，并指望这些选民不会惩罚他们？

sentences.en: Well, my guess is no, though, I suppose we'll find out soon enough.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的猜测是没有，不过我想我们很快就会知道了。

sentences.en: I mean, for most of these members, there are two big competing factors that, you know, shape this political moment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对大多数这些议员来说，有两个巨大的竞争因素，你知道，它们塑造了当前的政治时刻。

sentences.en: On the one hand, there's this wave of horrific violence,
sentences.zh: 一方面，是一波可怕的暴力浪潮，

sentences.en: which has led some number of Republican-leaning voters to say maybe we do need to do something about mass shootings and gun violence in the country.
sentences.zh: 这导致一定数量倾向于共和党选民表示，也许我们确实需要对国内的大规模枪击事件和枪支暴力做点什么。

sentences.en: And that, I think, has created, if not an easy path for Republicans to support new gun legislation,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，这为共和党人支持新的枪支立法创造了一条道路，即使不是一条轻松的道路，

sentences.en: has at least cracked the door open enough that maybe you at least want to wonder about what they would do in a way that two months ago wouldn't even be worth asking whether any Republican congressmen or senators would back new gun laws.
sentences.zh: 也至少把大门撬开了一点缝隙，也许你至少会想知道他们会怎么做，而在两个月前，甚至都不值得去问是否有任何共和党国会议员或参议员会支持新的枪支法律。

sentences.en: On the other hand, though, this has become, you know, a hot-button polarized issue at a moment when the country is deeply polarized.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，在国家深度两极分化的时刻，这已经成为一个高度敏感的两极分化议题。

sentences.en: This is, you know, it's Joe Biden who's pushing it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正是乔·拜登在推动此事。

sentences.en: Democrats are totally united on it.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在这个问题上完全团结一致。

sentences.en: And that tends to cut the other way.
sentences.zh: 而这往往会朝相反的方向发展。

sentences.en: For many people who might otherwise be on the fence, that political context can turn guns into, you know,
sentences.zh: 对于许多原本可能处于摇摆不定的人来说，这种政治背景会将枪支变成，你知道的，

sentences.en: just another blue versus red issue where people are going to want to rally around their team and deny a victory to the other side.
sentences.zh: 又一个蓝色对红色的议题，人们会想要团结在自己的阵营周围，并拒绝让另一方取得胜利。

sentences.en: I don't know exactly how that will shake out for any individual member,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这对于任何具体的议员来说会如何收场，

sentences.en: but I will say that at this moment in our country's history and with Joe Biden being as unpopular among Republicans as he is and the Democrats being as unpopular among Republicans as they are,
sentences.zh: 但我可以说，在我们国家历史的这一时刻，随着乔·拜登在共和党人中如此不受欢迎以及民主党人在共和党人中如此不受欢迎，

sentences.en: that it will always be a heavy lift to convince Republicans to join alongside Democrats on any of these culturally silent issues like guns.
sentences.zh: 要说服共和党人在枪支等任何这类文化敏感议题上与民主党人站在一起，总是需要付出巨大努力的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in a way, while it seems like precisely the moment for Democrats to be asking Republicans to vote for gun control, I mean, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，虽然这似乎正是民主党人要求共和党人投票支持枪支管控的时刻，我的意思是，你知道，

sentences.en: we just saw 19 schoolchildren shot to death in Uvalde, Texas.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚看到19名学童在德克萨斯州乌瓦尔德被枪杀。

sentences.en: For some, it might be precisely not the moment to do that because everybody's watching, right?
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，这可能恰恰不是做这件事的时刻，因为所有人的眼睛都在盯着，对吧？

sentences.en: And we are living in a world in which it's very difficult to go against your own team in favor of what the other team is doing.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个非常难以违背自己阵营去支持另一阵营所作所为的世界里。

sentences.en: And so the consequences of going against your own team would be severe.
sentences.zh: 因此，违背自己阵营的后果将是严重的。

sentences.en: Yeah, if you could create a political moment where Republicans wouldn't feel like they were having to support the Democrats or cave to a long-held Democratic view,
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你能创造这样一个政治时刻：共和党人不会觉得他们必须支持民主党人或向长期坚持的民主党观点妥协，

sentences.en: but still have all this attention on the issue, maybe that could create the conditions for a compromise or for more bipartisan movement.
sentences.zh: 但对这个议题仍然有这么多的关注，也许这可以为妥协或更多的两党合作创造条件。

sentences.en: But that's really hard to bring about.
sentences.zh: 但要实现这一点真的很难。

sentences.en: It's really hard to bring all of that attention to an issue without it plugging in to partisan politics as usual.
sentences.zh: 要将如此多的关注集中到一个议题上，而不让它陷入司空见惯的党派政治中，真的是难上加难。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the lights on this issue are so bright right now.
sentences.zh: 而且这个议题现在受到的关注实在是太耀眼了。

sentences.en: About as bright as it gets.
sentences.zh: 可以说是耀眼之极。

sentences.en: Nate, thank you.
sentences.zh: 内特，谢谢你。

sentences.en: No, thank you.
sentences.zh: 不，谢谢你。

sentences.en: On Monday, Senator Chris Murphy, a Democrat from Connecticut, said that a bipartisan group of senators is getting closer to an agreement on gun legislation
sentences.zh: 周一，来自康涅狄格州的民主党参议员克里斯·穆菲表示，一个两党参议员小组正在接近就枪支立法达成协议

sentences.en: that could include proposals on mental health, school safety, and background checks.
sentences.zh: 这可能包括关于心理健康、学校安全和背景调查的提案。

sentences.en: The lead Republican senator at the negotiating table, John Cornyn from Texas, has not committed to anything, but said that, quote, hope springs eternal.
sentences.zh: 谈判桌前的共和党首席参议员、来自德克萨斯州的约翰·科宁尚未做出任何承诺，但他表示，用他的话说，希望永存。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他消息。

sentences.en: On Monday, British Prime Minister Boris Johnson survived a no-confidence vote in Parliament.
sentences.zh: 周一，英国首相鲍里斯·约翰逊在议会的不信任投票中幸存下来。

sentences.en: The vote fell short of what was needed to oust Johnson as Tory party leader.
sentences.zh: 这次投票未达到将约翰逊赶下保守党党魁宝座所需的票数。

sentences.en: But it showed just how much support for him had dropped since last year,
sentences.zh: 但它表明，自去年以来，对他的支持率下降了多少，

sentences.en: when reports emerged that he and his aides threw parties that violated the government's COVID lockdown rules.
sentences.zh: 当时有报道称他和他的助手们举办了违反政府新冠封锁规定的派对。

sentences.en: Johnson argued that the vote should end months of speculation about his future.
sentences.zh: 约翰逊辩称，这次投票应该结束长达数月关于他未来的猜测。

sentences.en: But history shows that conservative prime ministers who've been subjected to such a vote, even if they win, are usually pushed out of office within a few months.
sentences.zh: 但历史表明，经历过此类投票的保守党首相，即使获胜，通常也会在几个月内被迫下台。

sentences.en: And five members of the far-right group, the Proud Boys, were indicted for seditious conspiracy in connection with the storming of the Capitol on January 6, 2021.
sentences.zh: 极右翼组织“骄傲男孩”的五名成员因涉嫌与2021年1月6日国会山骚乱有关的煽动性阴谋而被起诉。

sentences.en: The men are accused of using force to try to overthrow the government.
sentences.zh: 这些人被指控使用武力企图推翻政府。

sentences.en: It is the most serious charge in the Justice Department's case.
sentences.zh: 这是司法部案件中最严重的指控。

sentences.en: The Proud Boys' former leader, Enrique Tarrio, was not in Washington on the day of the assault.
sentences.zh: “骄傲男孩”的前领导人恩里克·塔里奥在袭击发生当天不在华盛顿。

sentences.en: But prosecutors said he, quote, led the advance planning and remained in contact with other members of the group during the storming of the building.
sentences.zh: 但检方表示，用他们的话说，他“领导了前期规划，并在大楼遭冲击期间与该集团的其他成员保持联系”。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Sydney Harper, Stella Tan, and Will Reed.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由悉尼·哈珀、斯特拉·谭和威尔·里德制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett, contains original music by Alicia Ba'itu, Marion Lozano, and Rowan Nemesto, and was engineered by Corey Schruppel.
sentences.zh: 节目由佩奇·考维特编辑，包含艾莉西亚·拜图、马里昂·洛萨诺和罗文·内梅斯托的原创音乐，并由科里·施鲁佩尔进行工程处理。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Bumberg and Ben Landsverk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由来自Wonderly的吉姆·布姆伯格和本·兰兹维克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》中，我们正在为假期招待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是全黑睡眠者吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们喝断片才能睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症、食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何地方查找《Wirecutter秀》。
